title: Why Run DuckDB Behind HTTP?
description: Wrap a single [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org) process in an HTTP endpoint so other services can `POST` SQL and read JSON back — no client driver, no separate query gateway. Best fit: a read-only DuckDB serving small internal APIs, BI dashboards, or [DuckDB-Wasm](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/wasm/overview) in a browser. **Not** a substitute for a hardened multi-tenant SQL gateway.

sections.title: What this extension is for
sections.description: Two SQL functions — `httpserve_start` and `httpserve_stop` — turn a running DuckDB into a tiny HTTP query service. The endpoint accepts SQL via `POST` body or `?query=` parameter, returns [JSON](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JSON), and ships an embedded browser UI called *quackplay*.

bulletPoints.label: Internal SQL APIs
bulletPoints.description: Stand up a JSON query endpoint over a curated DuckDB database file so other services can pull aggregates without a client library. Pair with `duckdb -readonly` for safe shared access.

bulletPoints.label: Ad-hoc browser exploration
bulletPoints.description: The built-in *quackplay* UI lets a teammate paste a query into a browser tab and see results — useful when shipping a DuckDB file is easier than shipping a BI tool.

bulletPoints.label: Cross-DuckDB query federation
bulletPoints.description: Each DuckDB process is reachable over HTTP from any other DuckDB. Combined with the [`chsql`](https://community-extensions.duckdb.org/extensions/chsql.html) extension's `duck_flock` macro, you can fan a single SQL statement out across multiple DuckDBs and merge the results.

bulletPoints.label: Glue for [DuckDB-Wasm](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/wasm/overview)
bulletPoints.description: A browser-side DuckDB can `POST` to a server-side DuckDB through this extension to pull canonical data without bundling it into the page.

sections.title: How it works
sections.description: `httpserve_start` spawns an HTTP listener thread inside the DuckDB process, owned by the calling connection. Requests are dispatched to the same DuckDB connection, so any state the connection has (`LOAD`ed extensions, attached databases, secrets) is visible to HTTP clients. There is one global server per process — calling `httpserve_start` twice replaces the listener.

bulletPoints.label: Endpoints
bulletPoints.description: `/` accepts `GET` and `POST` for query execution. `/ping` is a `GET` health check. There is no `/metrics`, no `/health`, no OpenAPI document — the API surface is intentionally small.

bulletPoints.label: Query input
bulletPoints.description: `POST` the SQL as the request body, or send it as `?query=` / `?q=`. `POST` is recommended once the SQL exceeds typical URL length limits.

bulletPoints.label: Response formats
bulletPoints.description: Pass `?default_format=JSONEachRow` for newline-delimited JSON ([JSONEachRow](https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/interfaces/formats#jsoneachrow)) or `JSONCompact` for a single document with `meta` / `data` / `rows` / `statistics` keys ([JSONCompact](https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/interfaces/formats#jsoncompact)). The format vocabulary intentionally mirrors the ClickHouse HTTP interface so existing tooling works.

bulletPoints.label: Authentication
bulletPoints.description: The third argument to `httpserve_start` is one of: empty string (no auth), `'user:pass'` ([HTTP Basic](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7617)), or any other value (treated as a single shared key sent in the `X-API-Key` header). There is one credential per server.

sections.title: Production caveats
sections.description: Exposing a SQL engine over HTTP is genuinely risky if you skip the boring parts. Read these before binding to a public interface.

bulletPoints.label: Run DuckDB read-only
bulletPoints.description: The endpoint executes whatever SQL it receives against the connection's full surface. Without `-readonly` (see the [DuckDB CLI docs](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/cli)), an authenticated client can `ATTACH`, `INSERT`, `COPY TO`, install extensions, or call file-system functions. The upstream README's first security note is exactly this.

bulletPoints.label: No built-in TLS
bulletPoints.description: The server speaks plain HTTP. Credentials and query results travel in the clear unless you front it with a TLS terminator like [nginx](https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_ssl_module.html), [Caddy](https://caddyserver.com/docs/automatic-https), or [HAProxy](https://www.haproxy.org/). [HTTP Basic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basic_access_authentication) without TLS is effectively no auth at all.

bulletPoints.label: One credential, no per-user scope
bulletPoints.description: Auth is binary: a request either presents the configured credential or it doesn't. There is no notion of users, roles, query allowlists, or rate limiting. For multi-tenant access, terminate auth at a gateway and run the server unauthenticated behind it on a private network.

bulletPoints.label: Lock down the DuckDB itself
bulletPoints.description: Even with `-readonly`, follow [DuckDB's hardening guidance](https://duckdb.org/docs/operations_manual/securing_duckdb/overview) — disable [community extension installation](https://duckdb.org/docs/operations_manual/securing_duckdb/securing_extensions), restrict filesystem access, and consider running the process inside a sandbox or container.

bulletPoints.label: Single process, no rate limiting
bulletPoints.description: Concurrency and throughput are bounded by what one DuckDB process can do. There is no built-in request queue, no per-client throttling, and no slow-query cutoff. Put a reverse proxy in front for any of those.

useCases.title: Read-only API in front of a curated DuckDB
useCases.description: Build a Parquet / CSV pipeline into a DuckDB file, attach it `-readonly`, `httpserve_start` on a private port, and let internal services `POST` aggregates. Front with TLS at the proxy.

useCases.title: Quick exploratory UI for a teammate
useCases.description: Open *quackplay* in a browser tab, paste queries, hand someone a URL. Cheaper than provisioning a BI seat for one-off questions.

useCases.title: Cross-DuckDB federation with `duck_flock`
useCases.description: Run `httpserve_start` on N DuckDB nodes, each exposing a slice of data, then use the [`chsql`](https://community-extensions.duckdb.org/extensions/chsql.html) extension's `duck_flock` from a coordinator DuckDB to fan queries out and merge results.

useCases.title: Backend for [DuckDB-Wasm](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/wasm/overview)
useCases.description: Let a browser DuckDB call `read_json_auto('http://server:9999/?q=...')` to pull authoritative data on demand instead of bundling it into the bundle.
